meaning: You bet, eighty thousand people a year wake up before the alarm and start counting what they have to carry. This seal, gold and small, is the hand on the back. Quiet. It stays.

Every family has an old door. Push it open, smell the food, the coat taken off your shoulders, no questions about the test. That door is not outside. It is inside. Auspicious Energy is not a god descending. It is you, finally living a life that smells that way.

english: Joy and Celebration Fill the Hall
meaning: Joy is not a promotion. It is Sunday morning, your partner in the kitchen, the child not crying, the light coming in. These moments are too rare to forget. This gold seal, it is the shape of that day, kept.

Summon Wealth sounds like superstition. You know it is not. What it really says is: you have to know the feel of money. The abacus, the ledger, the stack of coins. This card does not earn for you. It lets money recognize your hand.

Piling Gold, Accumulating Jade — the words are heavy on the tongue. There is no mountain of gold. It is one dollar a day, the thing you did not buy, the moment your salary lands and you held off. This card is the nod to that one second.

My parents generation cared about two things: blessings and longevity. But they never said it. This seal, you put it on their table when you go home for the new year. You say nothing. They read the four words. They know.

You feel health only after a certain age. Before thirty, late nights cost nothing. After thirty, one bad week of sleep scares you. Health and Peace is not about living long. It is about not trading your body for things not worth it. This gold seal, a reminder to ease up.

A Hundred Blessings Arrive. Too full, who believes it. I think it does not mean all will come. It means there is a chance at each. One more call, one more step, one breath swallowed. That is one of the hundred.

A Thousand Auspicious Signs is even more than a hundred. I think the old people wrote it for that feeling when one thing after another just goes right. These days are rare. But you have to recognize it. When it comes, do not look at the phone. Look up at the sky.

english: Gold and Jade Fill the Hall
meaning: Gold and Jade Fill the Hall is when a person is most full. The house is full, the cabinet is full, the head is clear. This seal in hand, it does not mean add more. It means: enough. Leave some space.

Great Fortune and Prosperity — who does not like it. But notice, it always has a scene: opening a business, traveling, starting work. Each scene has something to do. This seal is not wishing you luck. It is wishing you to move.

All Things Go Smoothly — too absolute, no one believes it. But some days, one email works, one sentence in a meeting lands, even the parking spot opens. That day is All Things Go Smoothly. This card tells you, that day will come again.
Wealth and Fortune Flow Freely — the key character is flow. Money does flow to you, just in pipes you cannot see. This seal, near the bank app icon, for each time you open it.

Great Fortune Is Upon You — dang tou (upon your head) is the most colloquial, most accurate — luck is on your head. This seal, for those whose day is not going well, but who look up at the clouds when they reach the bottom of their building.
Gold Pours In Daily — these four words are too full, but the ancients said them because they believed small adds up. This seal, on your coin jar or daily check-in of your accounting app.

english: Blessings Vast as the Eastern Sea
meaning: Blessings Vast as the Eastern Sea — the four characters read slow, but you want this slow. This seal, on the fridge door. Open it, see it.

english: Longevity Firm as the Southern Mountain
meaning: Longevity Firm as the Southern Mountain — the Southern Mountain, elders live to that age. This seal, on your parents nightstand, for those who hope for a few more years with them.

Heaven-Sent Good Fortune — these four characters are for those who have not met that person yet. Good fortune does not fall from the sky, it comes because while waiting, you made yourself ready. This seal, on the dresser or bedside.
Ample Clothing and Abundant Food — the most plain, most deserved. This seal, in the center of the dining table. The one who eats knows best what these four characters mean.
Peaceful Home, Joyful Work — peace first, joy after. The ancients wrote these four characters in order. This seal, inside the bedroom door.
Prosperous and Flourishing — prosper first, flourish after. This seal, at the bottom-left of your first sticky note or calendar.
Rising Steadily Day by Day — sounds like stocks, but the ancients said it for those who progress a little daily. This seal, on the small notebook you write in before bed.
Rising Step by Step — the character bu (step) is heaviest. Step by step. This seal, on the first stair at home. You step on it every day going up and down.
A Future Bright as Brocade — brocade is woven. This seal, on the innermost notebook on your desk, the one you cannot throw away.

english: All That You Wish Comes True
meaning: All That You Wish Comes True — heart first. The ancients said this because many wishes fail, the heart did not truly wish. This seal, on the cover of your New Year wish list.

When two people stop speaking, they think it is closeness. The chopsticks are set, the shoes are tidy, the silence is comfortable. But every now and then, you want to hear one specific thing. This seal, vermilion, sits in the book on your nightstand. It reminds you. Closeness is not spent. It is kept.

The paired birds share one wing. Neither can fly alone. This is not romance. It is a warning. Whoever you pick, you are tied for life. One wing breaks, you both fall. This seal is for the one still choosing.

Flowers Bloom, Moon Is Full — I thought as a child it was about scenery. Grown up, I know it is about people. Flowers at peak, moon at full, both cannot stay. This seal is for the kind of love that knows it will not stay, and still looks.

Twin Lotus, one stem two flowers, look the same. Look long, you see they face different ways. Love is like that. You think you are the same, but each heart has its own direction. This seal, the courage to accept that difference.

Bound Forever in Heart — you heard these four words on your wedding day, never again. But they are not for that day. They are for every day. One Heart is not given at the start. It is built in every fight. This seal by the bed, a reminder to bind again each day.

Branches Joined as One — two trees lean together, branches tangle with time. But notice, tangled or not, they are still two trees, roots apart. Love is not becoming one person. It is two whole people choosing the same posture.

Phoenixes Sing in Harmony — the ancients paired two birds. But I love the word sing. It is sound, it is you still willing to fight, to say something, to laugh. This seal, for the love that still talks.

Swallow and Oriole Pair — the words mean good birds in pairs. I think it means the light, un-tiring kind of company. Swallows and orioles are not heavy. They fly, they stop, they chirp. This seal, for the kind of relationship where seeing each other is enough.

Love Deep as the Sea — sea is the worst metaphor. Sea has tides, storms, ebb. But think the other way. Tide, storm, ebb, all still the sea. Love is the same. Deep is not unchanging. It is changing and still that person.

Eternal as Earth and Sky — these four words lied to many. The earth is 4.6 billion years old, one day it will not be. But that day not being is also part of Eternal. This seal, for everyone afraid of one day.

english: Vows as Vast as Sea and Mountain
meaning: Vows as Vast as Sea and Mountain — vows are cheap. But notice, those who trust vows least, swear the most. In love, what carries weight is not the I do, but the next ten years, every morning, choosing that person again. This seal under the bed, for those ten years.

Clinging as Glue and Lacquer sounds sweet. It is actually about over-fresh love. New love does. Five-year love does not. Real love is tired, is annoyed, is the evening when you look at the phone and he looks at his. This seal, for after the glue dries, when it is quiet and true.
Raising Trays to Eyebrow Height — the wife serves the husband, raising the tray to eyebrow height, respect. This seal, for everyone who cooks and serves for the one at home.
Mutual Respect as Guests — bin is guest. This seal, for those who treat their partner as a guest after ten years of marriage. This kind of relationship lasts longest.
Growing Old Together — white head is gray hair. This seal, for those who did not plan to grow old together but did.
One Heart, One Virtue — one heart is same heart, one virtue is same principle. This seal, for those who cannot say I was wrong in a fight, but can say I will do better next time.
Inseparable as Shadow Follows Form — shadow is shadow. This seal, for the kind of love that goes where you go, but you do not notice.

Hearts Connected at a Glance — ling is spirit, xi is rhinoceros. The ancients used an animal to name a feeling — the most expensive thing in the world is understanding without words. This seal, for those who fight, then a glance, then make up.
Morning and Evening, Forever — morning and evening. This seal, on the two drawers of the nightstand — one is theirs, one is yours.

Boundless Eternal Joy — wei yang means not yet ended. The ancients knew the words. They did not write forever happy. They wrote not yet ended. Joy breaks, but it comes back. This seal, for everyone whose joy broke and reconnected.

Joy Fills the Courtyard — the more you write the character 喜, the less real it is. Real joy is not how many 喜 characters you paste, it is the way your partner looks up when you walk in. This seal, on the key box by the door. So every homecoming carries it.

Reunion in Perfect Harmony — these four words weigh most in China. The train ticket home does not matter. What matters is your mother looking once and saying, you got thinner. This seal, for everyone far away. Reunion is being able to go back. Perfection is what stays in the heart.

Love Unchanging — unchanging is the heaviest word. In love, shifting is normal. Attention shifts, energy shifts, liking shifts. Unchanging is not never shifted. It is shifted and came back. This seal, for those who left and returned.

Together for a Lifetime sounds like a promise. It is a habit. The morning breakfast, waiting for them to shower, turning off the light before bed. Each is small. All together, a lifetime. This seal is not a promise. It is a habit.

Happiness Forever Dwells — forever is a lie. But you look at this card for three seconds, you believe. Three seconds is enough. To breathe, to loosen the brow, to say the next sentence well. This seal, for those three seconds.

You have been working hard for a long time. The overtime, the review, the thing you did not say. Direction, you realize, is not solved by trying harder. The Purple Star is the one fixed light. It shines on whoever sits down and admits what they have been waiting for.

The Northern Dipper Bestows Life — the ancients answer to where life comes from. Seven stars, ladle-shaped, turn over your roof every night. The ancients did not say they turn, they said they bestow — like a slow IV drip of life. This seal is not for long life. It is a reminder that you are still being bestowed.

The Southern Dipper Extends Life — paired with the Northern one, one rules birth, one longevity. The ancients wrote extend gently. Extend is not add, it is lengthen. Like smoothing a wrinkled paper. This seal, for those who want a few more years with their children, a few more years of being human.

Wen Chang rules study, writing, exams, interviews. This star, over a thousand years in China, every student who burned the midnight oil looked up at it. But you know today, Wen Chang does not take the test for you. It lets your heart settle the moment you sit down. This seal, for that one moment of sitting down.

Wu Qu is the sixth of the Dipper. The ancients said it ruled money, but Wu Qu does not give money directly. It gives the courage to ask. The salary you do not dare negotiate, the final payment you do not dare collect, the byline you do not dare claim. Wu Qu is that one second before you speak. This seal, for that one beat.

Tai Yin is the moon. The ancients paired the moon with protecting life, because the moon rules the night. The sun lights the day, the moon guards the night. When you cannot sleep, when you wake from a dream, when you drive home alone at night, this star is with you. This seal on the nightstand, the bright side facing you.

The Sun Shines Wide — the most ordinary star, also the most necessary. It rises every day, no one looks up, but it is there. Wide does not mean special light for someone. It means light for everyone. Ordinary days, ordinary life. Those without this star know. This seal, for your ordinary days.

Yu Heng is the fifth of the Northern Dipper. In astrology, it judges and weighs. The ancients invited this star near, usually on a night of guilty conscience. You have those nights too, when you did something you cannot explain. This seal does not acquit you. It lets you sleep a little better that night.

Tian Quan is the fourth of the Dipper. The ancients gave this star the role of establishing the pivot — the center. In every home, every company, one person is the center. But the center is not the most comfortable. It is the most tired. This seal, for everyone who has been the center, has been tired, has thought of quitting.

Tian Ji is the third of the Dipper. The ancients said it ruled strategy. But strategy is heavy. We ordinary do not strategize nations. Tian Ji for us is what to eat for dinner, which class for the child, do I switch jobs this month. Each small decision, a strategy. This seal, a little more respect for your own small strategies.

Kai Yang is the sixth of the Dipper. The ancients said it illuminated the world. These four words sound grand. On you, it is: late night coming home, the street lamps light up one by one, you look up at them. Each lamp is a Kai Yang. This seal, on the keychain, one look every day home.

Yao Guang is the last star of the Dipper. The ancients wrote lead the way, two plain words. Lead is lead, way is way, no adjectives. This seal, for everyone who does not know the next step. You do not need to know how long the road is. You only need the next step.

Gou Chen is a small square of six stars in the sky. The ancients paired it with governing the world. Not ruling, tending. Governing the world means sweeping the floor for the world. This seal, for those who cook for the child, change the medicine for the elder, scoop the litter for the cat. You govern the world every day.

Heavenly Market is one of the twenty-eight mansions. The ancients tied it to markets, merchants, trade. This star is not about earning more. It is about knowing in trade — what to sell what not, what price to give, what price to hold. This seal, in the inner pocket of the wallet. Open it, look once.

english: Purple Energy Ascends to the Heavens
meaning: Purple Energy Ascends to the Heavens — ling means to push up against, to surge. Purple energy is the highest auspicious sign in Daoism. This seal, for those pushing, carrying, surging toward something. You know what that thing is. I do not need to say.

The North Star Abides — the Pole Star. All stars move, only this one does not. The ancients called it where one abides. Whatever city you are in, whatever house, whatever seat, this seal says: your Pole Star does not need to be beautiful. It only needs to not move.

Tai Yi Casts Its Light — Tai Yi is the most honored in heaven. The ancients wrote casts light — chui means to lower. Light was in the sky. Tai Yi lowered it to the world. This seal, for everyone who lowers their light: teachers, doctors, parents, taxi drivers.

Three Platforms Guard — three groups of stars. The ancients used the word guard carefully. Not save, block. Guarding is someone blocks for you without you knowing. This seal, for those you have not met, but owe a thank you.

Heavenly Yi is the nobleman star. The ancients wrote Heavenly Yi Nobleman to admit a fact. You did not carry this life alone. Someone caught you at some point. This seal is a reminder — today too. Today you are someone else nobleman.

Canopy Covers from Above — the canopy is the umbrella over the emperor. This seal, hung in the car, protects the driver. Covers from Above means: however fast you drive, the canopy is over you. This seal, for everyone commuting every day.

Moonlight Flows Like Water — the ancients described moonlight as water, because water reflects all things. When you look at the moon today, you are not looking at the moon. You are looking at water. This seal, on the mirror. Every morning looking in, you remember: I am being reflected.

Stars Guide the Path — stars will not write you a full plan, but each is a small arrow. The person you meet today, the word you see, the sentence you hear, each is a star. This seal, to let you see the path through those small, seemingly unrelated arrows.

Cloud Path Reaches the Mysterious — cloud path is the road in the clouds. The ancients knew clouds are high, but the road in them reaches somewhere more mysterious. This seal, for those half-way and want to turn back. Where the road ahead leads, no one knows. But the road behind does not disappear.

Heaven Gate Reaches the Sacred — heaven gate is the door in the sky. The ancients said it opens for the sacred, not the clever. Sacred and clever are not the same. Clever is fast reaction. Sacred is far sight. This seal, for those who are not fast but see far.

Spirit Platform Clear and Bright — spirit platform is the heart. The ancients called the heart spirit platform — ling is sensitive, tai is steady. The heart both sensitive and steady, this is the hardest thing. This seal, for that moment before you sleep tonight: breath slow down, the platform clears itself.

Mystic Heaven Guards the Peaks — mystic heaven is the northern sky. The ancients felt the northern sky was solid, could press down on things. This seal, for those who can press down on things. You know how much you hold. This card does not unload you. It tells you: being able to press down has weight.

Thunder Command — Thunder Department is a law-enforcement team in heaven. The ancients wrote the two characters chi ling with the heaviest meaning. Chi is command, ling is execution. This seal, for those whose word counts. Every word you say is command. You know.

True Thunder Method — thunder is the sound of heaven. The ancients said true method is five kinds of rightful thunder. This seal, for those who have heard the truth. Real thunder does not sound good. But the crooked thing in you straightens.

Divine General Protects — divine general is a soldier in heaven. The ancients wrote protect body as close to the body. This seal, for that person next to you who has been protecting you, but you never knew.

Eight Powers Subdue Evil — wei is dignity, xie is evil. The ancients said eight dignity subdue eight evil. This seal, for the hard-boned. Hard-boned is not fierce. It is standing without leaning on others.

Six Ding Six Jia — these are the names of twelve protectors in Daoism. The ancients invited them home, pasted one on the door. This seal, for those whose home has rules. Rules are not cages. They are guardrails.
Seven Stars Cut Down Evil — the seven stars. The ancients called this group cut. Cut through. Evil is sha. This seal, for those who were chased by evil, but walked through.

Black Tortoise Guards the North — Black Tortoise is a turtle-snake god. The ancients placed it in the north, to guard the north. This seal on the north-facing window, for those whose north room is still lived in.

White Tiger Subdues the West — White Tiger is the main god of the west. The ancients used the word su heavily. Su is clearing the field. This seal, for those who close work outside the door when they leave. You need that clearing.

Azure Dragon Guards the East — Azure Dragon is the god of the east. The ancients called east the place of rising qi. This seal on the east-facing window, for those whose first morning light falls on the desk.
Vermilion Bird Burns Evil — Vermilion Bird is the fire bird of the south. The ancients used the word burn. Evil is not chased away, it is burned. This seal, for those who burn away the unkindness.
Flying Serpent Binds — flying serpent. The ancients felt serpents bind. So they used the word bind. This seal, for those bound by a relationship. Bound is not bad, but you have to know it is binding.

Gou Chen Guards the Center — Gou Chen is the star at the center. The ancients called center not leaning. This seal, for those who have walked long without leaning. You do not lean, but not leaning is tiring too.
Heavenly Dipper Righteous Energy — gang is upright. This seal, on the office desk, for those treated unfairly but did not bend.

Earth Fiend Protects — sha means fierce, earth fiend is the fierce on earth. But the ancients used protect dharma. Even the fierce protect dharma. This seal, for those treated fiercely, but still keep the rules.

Bright Hall Gathers Spirits — bright hall is the space in front of the forehead. The ancients said gather spirits is to gather in. This seal, where you look up before a meeting, for those who look at themselves first.
Jade Hall Pure and Solemn — Jade Hall is the Heavenly Emperor office. The ancients used two characters — qing is clean, su is solemn. This seal, for those whose home has quiet rules.

Dragon Abyss Subdues Evil — dragon abyss is the water bottom where dragons live. The ancients said dragons in the abyss do not fly, but the dragon in the abyss holds the water still. This seal, for those who do not show off, but know in their heart.
Tiger Roar Summons the Wind — when the tiger roars, wind comes. This seal, for those who do not talk much, but when they speak, the room goes quiet.
Golden Armor Divine Might — golden armor is the golden armor. This seal, for those who dress neatly to go out. Armor is not for others to see. It is for yourself.
Iron Walls Copper Fortress — the most ordinary words. This seal, for those whose wall, door, window is still there. The wall is there, the home is there.
Diamond Indestructible — diamond is the hardest in Buddhism. This seal, for those who have been hit, denied, deceived, but did not break.
Jade Pure Command — Jade Pure is one of the Three Pure Ones in Daoism. Chi is command. This seal, for those who keep the command they give themselves.
Supreme Pure Subdues Demons — Supreme Pure is the second of the Three. Zhen is to subdue. This seal, for those whose messy thoughts are subdued. Subduing is not killing, it is making them quiet.

Highest Pure Dispels Evil — Highest Pure is the third. Dang is to brush away. This last character of this seal, for those whose evil is brushed outside, not getting in. Door closed, window open one inch.

In the fixed edition, this was chosen because the pair holds up best. Two instruments, one key, neither pressing the other, two lines one ahead one behind. This seal, where both of you can see it. Not for one to yield, but to remember how the same rhythm began.

In the fixed edition, this was chosen because the four words suit a window best. Flower blooms, moon is full, you do not worry if it is the right time. This seal, on the window, a reminder: bloom when it blooms, be full when it is full.

In the fixed edition, this was chosen because it appears most on your wedding day. This seal, on the first page of the album or the highest point on the wall. It says nothing grand. It only says: you tied. Remember.
In the fixed edition, this was chosen because as people age, eyes are truer than words. This seal, next to the small frame on the nightstand. You wake, look once. No words needed.

In the fixed edition, this was chosen because jing (respect) is hardest. Qin (closeness) is instinct, jing is practice. This seal, on the most visible surface in the living room. Guests see it, no matter.
In the fixed edition, this was chosen because these four words weigh nothing the day you marry, only ten years later. This seal, on the innermost wall of the master bedroom. One look before bed.

In the fixed edition, this was chosen because de (virtue) is principle. A couple is not just one heart, but one virtue — one judgment. This seal, under the paper where you write New Year wishes each year.

In the fixed edition, this was chosen because wei yang (not yet ended) is the most wonderful. At home, child, elder, that moment of laughter not yet finished. This seal, on the small table in the living room. The whole family sees.
In the fixed edition, this was chosen because the character 喜 is pasted. Chinese paste 喜 for New Year, to invite joy from outside in. This seal, inside the door. The one who opens sees it first.

In the fixed edition, this was chosen because this dining table is the heaviest for Chinese. The whole year, for that one meal. This seal, in the center of the dining table. The whole family faces it when they eat.

In the fixed edition, this was chosen because bu yi (unchanging) takes enduring. This seal, on the back of your first photo frame. The frame faces out, the back faces the wall — but you know it is there.
In the fixed edition, this was chosen because yong zhu (forever dwells) takes a little doing every day. This seal, on the kitchen wall — the one who cooks knows best what forever dwells means.
In the fixed edition, this was chosen because Monday morning, you face the numbers. This seal, at the bottom-left of your computer screen.
In the fixed edition, this was chosen because saving is daily. This seal, on your piggy bank or the first page of your ledger.

english: Gold and Jade Fill the Hall
meaning: In the fixed edition, this was chosen because full hall is not crammed, it is in order. This seal, on the cleanest corner of your desk.
In the fixed edition, this was chosen because the second before leaving home is most useful. This seal, at the bottom-right of the small entry mirror.
In the fixed edition, this was chosen because you do not lack goals, you lack not getting stuck. This seal, at the top-left of your first sticky note each day.
In the fixed edition, this was chosen because connections are also fortune. This seal, above the first page of your phone book or WeChat contacts.
In the fixed edition, this was chosen because luck is not waited for, it is worn. This seal, inside your wardrobe door.
In the fixed edition, this was chosen because 15 minutes daily beats 10 hours on weekends. This seal, on your desk lamp base.
In the fixed edition, this was chosen because the cleanness of the work space affects luck. This seal, on the top layer of your file rack.
In the fixed edition, this was chosen because one small step daily beats one big step yearly. This seal, on the last page of your calendar.
In the fixed edition, this was chosen because rising is not climbing stairs, it is switching lanes. This seal, on the folder you open before switching jobs.

english: All That You Wish Comes True
meaning: In the fixed edition, this was chosen because you have to first think clearly. This seal, on the cover of your New Year wish list.
